prompt:
Locked-off camera. The grey-haired man in the olive waterproof sits at a small round pub table, centre, right hand resting on the tabletop beside a pint and a red cup; the blurred tweed shoulder of another drinker fills the left foreground. He says "So why can't we?" quietly and deadpan, at a natural pace, face barely moving, then stops and takes a small look round: eyes to the man in the foreground, then across to his other side, then back. Mouth closed after the line. Only his mouth moves for words; the foreground shoulder stays still. Same room, same warm light, only the people already in the frame, the picture clean. Small, real pub performance; photographic.
Thanks.
